nodes.label: Prior-based lens mass estimate (M_lens)
nodes.rationale: Pairs each posterior tE sample with Monte Carlo draws from assumed mu_rel (log-normal) and D_L (naive uniform line-of-sight, not a real Galactic density model) priors, since tE alone can't fix mass. Explicitly flagged as the single biggest caveat in the pipeline and only illustrative, not a real mass measurement.

nodes.label: Mass-distance-velocity degeneracy (central open question)
nodes.rationale: tE alone conflates the angular Einstein radius and relative proper motion, so it can't fix a lens mass or distance without finite-source effects, parallax, or independent proper motion -- this is exactly why brown-dwarf-mass lenses are hard to identify from microlensing alone; the whole project exists to make this degeneracy visible, not hide it behind a point estimate.

nodes.label: mcmc_fit.estimate_mass()
nodes.rationale: Pairs each posterior tE sample with a Monte Carlo draw from assumed mu_rel/D_L priors to produce a full M_lens distribution rather than a point estimate, directly answering session 1's central open question. Flagged with a ponytail comment that the uniform-D_L/fixed-D_S prior is a naive line-of-sight prior, not a real Galactic density model; a disk/bulge-weighted prior (Han & Gould 2003) is the documented upgrade path if the mass distribution's shape ever needs to be quantitatively trustworthy.

nodes.label: O-03-BLG235 calibrate-once-then-fit pipeline
nodes.rationale: OGLE and MOA report incompatible units with no valid direct conversion, so a single shared-trajectory fit (fit_joint_pspl) is run once to solve fs_ogle/fb_ogle/fs_moa, then both instruments are inverted onto a common magnification scale A(t). This freezes the flux calibration at a point estimate, which session 5/6 showed can be measurably biased (chi2 31,982 vs 1,953) for a real caustic-crossing trajectory not seen during calibration.

nodes.label: /grill-me consensus mechanism
nodes.rationale: Used to reach consensus before acting on any new want not already in CHANGELOG.md, and to confirm next-session goals during 'save state'. Session 11 found diminishing returns in running further grill-me rounds once real run results already answered the practical question -- a direct decision from someone who saw the results was judged faster and no less valid.

nodes.label: Huber loss likelihood (2L1S track)
nodes.rationale: Tried as the first well-documented alternative to Student-t for the 2L1S track's caustic-spike problem, with DELTA=1.345 fixed (not fit) so it needs no normalizing-constant correction; ultimately found (with chi2 and Student-t) to fail to fit the caustic spike at all, so parked rather than pursued further.

nodes.label: Student-t robust likelihood
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Huber/sigma-clipping because a residual diagnostic on O-05-BLG086 showed a globally heavier-than-Gaussian error distribution (excess kurtosis 1.23, dof~6 MLE) rather than a small population of discrete outliers -- a smooth down-weight fits the observed error shape better than a hard/linear cutoff.

nodes.label: Wrong-but-plausible convergence pattern
nodes.rationale: A recurring failure mode identified across multiple independent sessions: a fit or result that looks converged, clean, and quantitatively fine by its own metric (chi2/dof, posterior shape, unimodality) is actually wrong, and only an independent, out-of-band check (a second instrument's data, a geometric image-count invariant, a known-correct comparison value, or a second implementation's own convention audit) reveals it. Seen in the u0-sign mirror-image bug (session 1), the OGLE-only single-lens misfit to a real binary event (session 1/2), the MulensModel coordinate-convention bug (session 3), and the near-miss-cusp caustic check (session 4).

nodes.label: User-writes/Claude-reviews collaboration mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode: Claude gives direction/hints and lets the user write the implementation, then simplifies with ponytail afterward. Explicitly and deliberately overridden several times (sessions 3, 5, 9) for specific pieces where Claude implemented directly instead, each logged as a scoped, one-off exception rather than a standing change.

nodes.label: Near-miss-cusp search-landscape problem
nodes.rationale: Under the fixed-then-fixed flux calibration, multi-start and most MCMC 2L1S searches converge to non-physical trajectories that never cross the caustic (no 3->5 image-count transition) yet score numerically better on chi2/Student-t/Huber than Bond et al.'s own published, genuinely-crossing solution -- only catchable via the image-count invariant check, not from the loss value alone. Session 11 found all three tried likelihoods disagree with each other on fitted parameters far more than a likelihood-shape difference should cause, pointing at this search-landscape issue as the dominant open problem rather than loss-function choice.
